state: I'm just here for the Brown Butter Almond Brittle, the best thing since sliced bread. After attending a Yelp event where my only regret was not choosing three servings of this ice cream. Needless to say that I found myself here again not long after. Don't be intimidated by the line outside of the door at Jeni's. It's only that way because there isn't much room inside for a line. They should consider getting those line makers that they have at the movie theatre so people aren't outside in the blistering heat. The lines move quick and the staff is very kind and diligent about moving customers down the counter, as there are three identical ice cream stations. I later went on a mission to find the ice cream in stores. Pints were $8 at Publix.

state: Small shop with a lot of variety. They have a lot you can park in and a couple of tables with benches outside. Inside is just the baked goods, no area for seating. Baked goods: ranged from cake slices, macarons, to pastries. We shared: - lobster tail: crunchier than I expected but I enjoyed it a lot. The cream filling is light, airy, and not overly sweet. Together, my husband described it like eating cereal. With the almost milky creaminess from the whipped cream and the crunchy pastry shell - New York crumb cake: was worried the crumbs would be the only good part but the cake is very moist and good! Overall a solid cake - horn (strawberries and cream): my least favorite, the pastry tasted undercooked. It was almost good. The filling seemed like it was just packaged strawberry cream cheese.

state: I had high hopes since many people would hype this place up but when I went I wasn't impressed. Personally what you get for the price point is not worth it in my opinion. We paid a little over $14 for the s'more sundae and strawberry shortcake sundae. First they didn't have the chocolate for the s'mores sundae so I had to substitute that. It came with one scoop of ice cream and a heaping of marshmallow fluff with one graham cracker broken in half. I did like that they toasted the fluff. Nothing wowed me from it. I've had better. Now for my husband's strawberry shortcake sundae. It was a flop. The "cake" was dry, hard, and almost old. It was as if they left it sitting out all day. You needed that ice cream to help get the cake down. The strawberries were hard and frozen and neither of us were a fan of that. We wish they would put fresh strawberries instead. They didn't put enough of the strawberry drizzle. What you see in the picture is all that was put on it. Again it was only one scoop of ice cream used. Honestly it's was an okay experience. The employees were friendly but were rushing us and the people before us. I will say if you want more for your money and better flavors, I recommend going elsewhere, like down the street to Nami!

state: I don’t like to be pessimistic, and maybe I chose the wrong flavor, but I was disappointed with the brownie ice cream! The sign in front is confusing—it says “Ohio City Ice Cream Co.” or something like that, but actually it’s from Mason’s. The ice cream had a very fresh taste, but not very tasty. The staff were very friendly and attentive, and the building is quite small, but it’s pretty charming, as you would expect for the area. state: If you're looking for delicious baked goods, there’s no need to look anywhere else! Upon entering, you can pick up a tray and tongs, then start selecting your favorite items. They offer a wide range of breads, from sweet ones to savory ones. The prices range from $1 to $3 per unit. We bought various types of bread, such as chocolate cookies and salted butter bread. Some breads have sweet fillings, while others are just simple, delicious savory breads. The place was very crowded when we arrived, but the line moves quickly. Once you move a little further along the line, someone will pack the bread individually for you. They also sell various cheesecakes, pastries, and drinks. Each pack of bread comes with a label indicating what it is and whether it contains eggs or milk. We bought about 7 different types of bread and a mini cheesecake soufflé, totaling around $20. This place offers a great variety of breads, sweets, and drinks. This is a must-visit if you travel to Las Vegas!

state: Ice cream is one of my favorite food groups. If you want to try amazing and diverse flavors of ice cream and sorbets—like taro, flan, halwa, Brie, and jam… Mason’s is the right place for you. They allow you to try any flavor you want, and with so many interesting options, it’s a great opportunity to choose what you really like. They get the flavors right! The staff is friendly and attentive, which is a big plus. As I said, I love ice cream, and if you gave me a bucket of vanilla ice cream, I would be very happy… but the ice creams at Mason’s are always a flavor adventure. What impresses me most, though, are Mason’s events and social activities. They have ramen nights, outdoor movie screenings in summer, and fundraising events with exclusive flavors and foods (please bring back the chocolate stick and peanut butter cream!). I brought my bike for maintenance there in exchange for a donation to help a girl who suffered a serious bicycle accident. All of this is more impressive than anything I could eat. I love supporting local businesses and important causes, and if I have to eat ice cream along the way… I’ll enjoy every bite!

state: From outside the city, we came to visit them based on the excellent recommendations from my Yelp friends. The reviews are very accurate. The place is located in a corner, and although the exterior looks a bit old-fashioned, don’t let that deter you. They only accept cash payments, so make sure you have enough money on hand. It costs about $11 per dozen, which is a great deal for homemade and fresh donuts. We bought a dozen different varieties. The chocolate glazed donuts were delicious, with a slight crunchy texture on the outside. The chocolate glazed donuts are super tasty—I really liked the thick chocolate glaze and the wonderful whipped cream topping. The bacon and maple donuts were a perfect combination of salty and sweet flavors, with fresh bacon pieces and maple glaze on a yeast dough donut. These yeast dough donuts aren’t the typical yeast dough donuts; they’re perfectly glazed and have a almost creamy texture. So, just heat them up in the microwave for 10 seconds, and you’ll appreciate them later. The German chocolate donuts are a chocolate cake with a walnut/coconut glaze and a wonderful layer of chocolate cream. My only concern is that there are no labels on any of the donuts. This is fine for regular visitors, but it makes it difficult to choose without bothering the staff and people behind you. However, this shouldn’t deter you at all. Donuts are definitely a must-visit!

state: I saw that they had French macarons the size of a hand, and I knew I had to buy them before leaving Las Vegas. I had never seen French macarons this big before, and the price wasn’t too expensive—just $3.50 per unit (compared to the small and expensive bites I’m used to). They didn’t have as much cream, and the outer layer was a little harder than what I’m used to, but they were still light and crunchy. I liked them for their size and flavor, but not as much as other ones I’ve tried.

state: I love this ice cream shop! When you enter, you’re always greeted with a smile. They have a variety of desserts that can satisfy any sweet craving. All the ice creams are made homemade, and they always have some new and interesting flavors. The staff is always patient when it comes to letting you try all the ice creams before you make up your mind. They always have a special ice cream for people over 21, which makes you feel special. The seating area at the back is limited, but it’s charming, with some counters and round tables. On some days, they offer flavored water for free, and I always love that.

state: So delicious! It was absolutely tasty! I got this recommendation from a Pinterest blog, and it was worth it. It’s a small store with many ice cream options and a wide variety of sweets. They make their own “marshmallow cream,” which is why I wanted to go there in the first place. It’s my favorite ice cream. We ordered a “s’mores sundae” to share, and it was huge and really good. They put a generous amount of “marshmallow cream” on it and toasted it. Usually, I prefer it hotter and melted, like a syrup, but this one was also very good. The service was excellent. They have a small backyard where we could sit and eat our ice cream. It’s a great place if you’re in the area!

state: We entered right when they were about to close. Only a few cannoli were left, so we bought them along with other cookies, cheese cake, brownies, and coffee. Everything seemed delicious. I chose the cheese cake—by the way, it’s just a cake without a base. It was amazing! It’s a small and cozy place, and it seems like one of those places that fill up quickly, with a long line, but not on a cold and snowy night. Again, it was almost time to close, but the staff wasn’t upset at all. They came over and asked if we needed boxes or anything else. They were very kind and also thanked us when we left.

state: Worth the hype worth the drive worth the wait... strawberry pop tart donut was as big as my hand definitely shareable. It's filled with strawberry and has the topping of a pop tart on top if your a fan of strawberry and donut plus pop tarts this was a great marriage. If you want a less massive donut and love apple or apple pie the apple crumb is the way to go the cake donut apple flavor again was great and my son even saved half for next day (still good) I also had a iced chai latte with almond milk and dash of cinnamon (didn't make the picture) perfect amount of chai to milk sometimes the spice from the chai can be over powering but this was great ( only regret was not getting a larger size) Customer service y'all know I love a good customer service.. they were friendly (the man plus women) sorry might even be the owner. But friendly, patient and did not rush me as I slowly looked. I was sad because the (FRENCH TOAST DONUT) served isn't during the week but if you go Saturday you can get it. Transportation I came from the strip and rode the deuce bus all the way to Fremont experience and just walked no more then 2 blocks they have a little back seating area then we walked back to Fremont st and saw the sights. When I'm back in Vegas this will be my stop!

state: I ordered a milk shake with cereal for myself, and a chocolate ice cream with pretzels for another person. I didn’t have any problems with the ice cream, but the milk shake with cereal wasn’t very good. It had a taste of old, spoiled milk, and it wasn’t even completely full in the glass. It wasn’t worth the price. I ordered the milk shake with cereal at the counter; it should have cost $7.5, but they charged $9 for the chocolate ice cream with cereal. I realized this only after they prepared it. I reported the problem, and they got angry because they made the wrong order. They prepared the correct drink for me, but in anger, they offered me the wrong drink for free. I hesitated to accept it, as they were upset about offering it for free. Then, even more angrily, they said, “Oh, you don’t want it for free?” Before I could respond, I took the wrong drink and left. As I was leaving, they stared at me and my family, and they kept commenting on me and my family. It was extremely rude. The wrong drink was just chocolate syrup.

state: Okay, so my best friend and I decided to buy something sweet. I myself aren’t really a fan of cakes or cupcakes, but I decided to ask her what she recommended. Let’s give it a try. We entered the store, and it was pleasant, clean, and inviting. Although it took a little while for us to be served, it wasn’t a problem, because we were distracted by the delicious food. There’s a wide variety of special and classic cupcakes. At first, I thought, “Well, I’ll get a chocolate one, since I love chocolate.” When we went to the counter to order, the staff took my friend’s order, giving me the last chance to look at the menu. I must say, I was so excited that I shouted, “I can’t believe it! They only serve cream!” My friend laughed, because I was so enthusiastic, and the staff just smiled, as if they were happy. Sorry to the couple who entered the store at that exact moment! Anyway, I decided to ask the staff to make sure the menu was correct. She confirmed that they only serve cream. With bright eyes, I ordered, “Please, two chocolate ones with sprinkles!” Because of this, this place has become my favorite place to go back to. It’s good to know that I wasn’t judged for not liking cakes. In many places, people ask, “What’s wrong with you, not liking cakes?” I didn’t receive any strange looks or comments, which made me very happy. Another reason is that the small bottles of cream cost only 75 cents each. So, it’s a win for everyone. Therefore, the only thing I can’t evaluate is the taste of the cupcakes themselves. But my friend said that she and her friends really like them. So, if the local residents like them, I will like them too! So, if you don’t like cakes, you definitely should come here!

state: I’m really into donuts, and the Donut Bar just makes things worse. The first time I went there, they had a promotion with birthday-themed donuts. I ordered one of those, plus a donut inspired by Homer Simpson. The waitress put two birthday-themed donuts in my box instead of one, as a special surprise, since it was the first week of operation, along with the Homer-themed donut. When I said it was also my birthday and that was great, she added another donut to the box! I’ve been back several times already, and I still haven’t gotten any donuts for free. However, I must say that the service was also very attentive! I recommend trying the chocolate milk or coffee options, and don’t forget to use the bathroom – at least check it out before leaving. The restaurant itself is quite small, so please explore the patio area for more places to sit, which are especially pleasant on spring and summer mornings.

state: Presti's is a place that you have to go to if you're in Little Italy. There's a reason most people rave about it. I've been here around dinner time on weekends and most recently around lunch time during a week day. The good part about going during the week, especially before 3 or 4, is that you avoid the lines because yes, Presti is popular and there will be lines. There's a reason they tell you to grab a number. However, despite how daunting a line you may encounter - it never takes long to get through it and the end result is worth the weight. The staff if cheerful, helpful and quick without making you feel rushed and unwanted. The cannolis are great - the shell is crispy (the ones covered in chocolate are extra amazing) and the cream is perfect. I came with a friend and she raved about it between bites. Their vast assortment of cookies are amazing. Because of its size, Presti's can afford to have a lot of variety so there will literally be something for everyone. I'm partial to their Linzer cookies, both the apricot and the raspberry. They're especially good when paired with their coffee. This time around I got a mocha which was a bit too sweet for my taste but that may have been because I downed two co okies with it so take that as you will. Next time I think I'd follow my friend's lead and grab a latte - still delicious but not sweet. Apart from the baked goodies there's also several options for lunch or dinner including strambolies, pizza, pasta, etc.. I eyed the Spinach stramboli but decided against it this time around. The strambolies have the perfect ratio of filling-to-bread so it was hard to walk away. I will be back though and that stramboli will be mine. The interior of this place as a whole is unsuprisingly large. There are numerous tables where you can eat comfortably with a large group or just by yourself. I saw several people at individual tables sipping their coffees and working on their laptops. The entire front of the bakery is windows so the natural light is always there and always pleasant, especially on a good day. Or you could always grab a seat in their patio area out front. Not going to lie, sitting out there and watching the people walk by as I sipped my coffee and nibbled on my treat brought back the feeling of sitting at a cafe in Europe. It was bright and breezy and the people walking past spoke a mix of English and Italian. These same people, more often then not, popped inside to grab a coffee or pastry as well. When the locals stop by you know it's worth it.

state: Very cute little shop in a nondescript location. The inside is super cute, bright, colorful, and cheery. I love the fact that they sell a lot of their homemade candies, marshmallows, cookies etc. and they are all displayed and packaged very nicely. Now on to the ice cream! The selection of flavors is varied, but not overwhelmingly huge like a lot of places can be. They have sorbets on one side of the counter, and their ice creams on the other. I didn't try any of the sorbets, but they looked great. While the menu had a ton of great looking sundaes to choose from, I ended up creating my own. I got a scoop of the espresso, and salted butter caramel with salted caramel sauce, toffee butter crunch, whipped cream, and a toasted marshmallow to top it off! The blend of flavors all together was excellent. Individually the components of the sundae were even better. You can tell the ice cream is handmade, quality stuff. The espresso was smooth, and the salted butter caramel my favorite, though I didn't quite taste the "salted" part that much. The toffee butter crunch was definitely one of my favorite parts of the sundae, and I could have probably just eaten a bag of that. The salted caramel sauce complimented the ice cream and was super tasty. The grand finale of the toasted marshmallow made for a great presentation, though it was difficult to eat in conjunction with the ice cream, and I actually ended up taking it off and eating it separately. It could have been toasted more, but that would obviously have made the ice cream underneath it melt even more than it started to. I will definitely be coming back here and trying more things. I did also try a sample of the honey blue cheese, and it was tasty and unique, but not something I could eat a whole scoop of!

state: I discovered this place last night. I can’t believe what I heard from the owner. The great staff at SuperFarm SuperTruck do more than just offer amazing Superfarm ice cream… no, no, no… they offer a huge variety of flavors. Does anyone know where to find it? YES! Let’s talk about this new ice cream shop, Melt. ~The Positive Points~ Well, the owner is a friend of the owner of Superfarm. I just realized that Udder Delights is also part of the ice cream network… so if you like Udder Delights, it’s worth visiting this place too! I love the variety of everything. A guy opened a small ice cream shop right next to Lost Leaf, and by chance, they have delicious local ice creams and Superfarm flavors… UNRECOGNIBLE!!! They have a huge variety of flavors. Currently, they have many ice creams and fruit-flavored ones. Of course, they also have traditional flavors like chocolate, mint chocolate, etc… but hey, they have Superfarm, which is an almond chocolate and Nutella ice cream—delicious! Just that ice cream alone is enough reason to come here. Instead of looking for the Superfarm truck or going to Gilbert, COME HERE! The owner is also very relaxed; it’s a real small business. They also make smoothies with the fresh ice creams from the farm. Just come and try it—you’ll love it. ~The Negative Points~ Actually, there aren’t many negative points. It’s not in a very nice building; it’s in a renovated house, like those you find in Roosevelt Row. There are no tables inside, so it can get warm if you eat outside. It’s more like “just go ahead” if you eat during the day. In my opinion, this place is great for evenings. It’s in Roosevelt Row, and not everyone likes that. If you like adding toppings and sides, they don’t offer those yet, so keep that in mind if it’s important to you. ~The Secrets~ Overall, this is a solid place, with 4 stars. The great and welcoming service, the variety of flavors, the freshness of ingredients, and the fact that the ice cream is made locally—all contribute to 4 stars. Is it a fancy place for “hipsters”? No. It’s a store that serves only local and fresh ingredients made on the farm? YES. Even the most traditional local stores don’t use such fresh ingredients. Melt is open from 12 noon to 12 noon, ALL DAY… So you can enjoy the ice cream whenever you want! Melt has the approval seal from the boss! Come and enjoy it!

state: But, of course, let’s give it 3.5 stars because it’s a fun concept. Our friends enjoyed a concert at Planet Hollywood and walked all the way to Cosmo in an effort to find the cereal ice cream and oat cake. The line was incredible, even at 10 p.m. We ordered exactly what we wanted, plus a oat cookie to share. As for the cereal ice cream, I’ve never been a big fan of corn cookies; but I understand the contrast. I think nostalgia is worth it, and probably the price is more related to the aesthetics. state: Melt is a great place to go for decent ice cream and unique flavors! They got rid of their six flavor sampler, but you really can't go wrong here. Their horchata flavor was amazing and I haven't had a bad cereal flavor yet. With that said, the comments about there being pieces of ice crystals in the ice cream are accurate. Sure, it doesn't compromise the flavor, but it does show it's not the best made ice cream in town. Also, I don't really get the novelty of the ice cream coming in Chinese take-out boxes, but some people really get a kick out of it. Lastly, street parking can be rough to find some nights (but hey, it is downtown Phoenix so what do you expect). This place is definitely worth checking out because of the unique flavors and convenience, but Melt and Mary Coles are close to downtown too and they might be better!

state: Personally, after dinner at Lola’s, I didn’t have any room in my stomach for dessert. But my sister insisted that we go to this place. It looked like a factory. You order your ice cream from one side of the glass, and on the other side, you see the workers preparing your ice cream. I wasn’t sure if I liked the atmosphere there, because it felt very industrial and a bit cold. The ice cream was good, and the portions were generous. However, I’ve tried better ice creams before, and this didn’t really feel like the ideal choice. We tried several flavors, but none stood out particularly. I prefer Jeni’s, and since I’m not from Columbus, I can’t say it’s a local product. But I knew it was a bad sign, because my sister, who loves ice cream, didn’t even finish hers! Instead, she left it on the armrest next to my phone, waiting for me to put my fingers in the ice cream. What disgusting!

state: Wow! I’m very happy to have had the opportunity to visit this place while we changed hotels, from the old Las Vegas to the new one during our trip. My husband and I went in for a “light” breakfast, knowing we had plans to go to a buffet later. But I greatly underestimated how delicious the desserts at this place were. The variety of donuts they offered was fantastic; it was hard to choose just a few (which was great, as we ended up with some extra options as well). Coming from the northeast, my favorite was the Maple Bourbon donut—it was very big, fluffy, and had just the right amount of frosting. My husband loved the Red Velvet one, and we also enjoyed some donuts with blue frosting and Halloween-themed decorations, as well as another giant donut with chocolate filling. I’m not one for drinking coffee, but they said it’s delicious. The parking on the street made it easy to get in and out. Our leftovers turned into a delicious treat after a late-night concert (and they assured us that the quality would stay good for up to 24 hours). The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful, and they took time to review all our options. An essential place in Las Vegas. It can be said to be one of the best donuts I’ve ever tried in my life.

state: Over the years, I’ve heard many positive things about Sweet Republic, but I always thought it was a difficult place to get to. The traffic near Shea and Loop 101 is very heavy during the day and after work hours. However, I finally decided to go there at 9 p.m., on a Saturday, when the streets should be empty. Thankfully, they were, as I needed to make a turn to enter the shopping center that houses Sweet Republic. Outside, there’s plenty of parking space, along with some tables and chairs in the open area. The interior is well-lit, with various tables, chairs, and seating areas in a cozy style. There are two display windows with fresh ice cream, a section with delicious toppings, and a freezer with ready-made ice cream containers. Oh, and there’s also a game area where you can pick up an old board game and play with friends. When I first entered, I wasn’t sure where to start. Although there’s a list of flavors and items available (sundae, milkshakes, coffee, etc.), I felt I needed to look at the ice cream first to get a better idea of what I wanted to eat. After trying a few flavors, my husband chose coconut and lemon in a waffle bowl. I opted for coffee ice cream with caramel pieces, salty caramel syrup, and a freshly baked marshmallow on top. It was delicious! (I’m obsessed with marshmallows, and this was amazing.) There were so many flavor options and types of sundae. I would love to go back and try all the other options. I’m sure I’m happy that I finally got to try it!

state: I ordered a cake for my husband’s 50th birthday two weeks before our trip to Las Vegas. When I went to pick up the cake on the day we arrived, they had no record of my order. They didn’t have any cakes available, but they could make one for pickup the next day—but it wouldn’t be a custom cake, as they needed an order two days in advance. I had already placed the order two weeks ago!!!! The next day, I got a generic cake, and I had to sign two documents that basically state that, regardless of the issue, I won’t be able to get a refund. Now I understand why they ask me to sign those documents—the cake was awful. I expected to receive a wonderful cake, like those from “Buddy the Cake Boss,” and I find better cakes at Costco. What a disappointment—and a waste of time and money. I should have ordered it at the Venetian hotel.

state: I used to get a dozen cupcakes from Sprinkles from a friend from L.A. who never seems to remember which flavors he gets me. The cupcakes pretty much all look the same which my friend describes as "cupcakes with nipples". They have regular-sized cupcakes as well as mini cupcakes. They have regular cupcakes, sugar-free cupcakes, and vegan/gluten-free cupcakes. There's a separate door/line for cupcakes, and ice cream shop. You can go to The Linq and get your cupcakes or order online. They deliver for a fee. You can sign up for their rewards program. My last bakery box include: 1 banana, 4 banana dark chocolate, 1 black & white, 1 black velvet, 1 chai latte, 1 chocolate marshmallow, 1 cinnamon sugar, 1 lemon coconut, 2 salty caramel, 1 sprinkle, 1 strawberry, 2 sugar free red velvet, 1 vanilla milk chocolate. But my absolute favorite is banana dark chocolate. It's like banana bread in cupcake form with delicious dark chocolate on top. Sooooo good! However, it's one of the flavors that's not available daily. Meaning, you have to check the schedule and see what days certain flavors are available. You can purchase cupcake mixes, cupcake stands, shirts and other merch. I could use some banana dark chocolate cupcake right about now...

state: It’s overrated! Very disappointing. My daughters and I were huge fans of “Cake Boss”, so visiting Carlos’s place was essential during our trip to Las Vegas. The line wasn’t bad, but the ordering and payment process was very inefficient. You choose what you want, and then you have to wait for someone to pack it for you. I had to try their famous red velvet cupcake. It wasn’t special at all, and the frosting needed much more sugar. It tasted similar to cream cheese. My daughter tried a clam… but it was too filled with filling, making it unpleasant. My other daughter ordered a mini cheese cake, which was too sweet. I usually don’t write negative reviews, but this is the first time… I feel disappointed because we wasted time and money on products of such mediocre quality.

state: A few years ago, a friend gave me some birthday cake balls from Milk Bar. Since then, they’ve become my favorite snack. I hoped to visit the New York branch when I went there, but unfortunately, I couldn’t do it during that busy trip. I invited my friend to come over after we ate at Momofuku. Even though she was “very satisfied,” she still managed to enjoy one of the birthday cake balls from the three-unit package. My friend shared her opinion about the “crack” cake—she highly recommended it, as it’s what they’re known for. I bought a slice; it was delicious, but I definitely prefer the birthday cake balls. They’re the best desserts there are (sorry, but the bundt cakes can’t compare—you’re in second place). We also tried the “crack” ice cream; we were lucky and didn’t have to wait in line. It had the same flavor as the “crack” cake, though I don’t know if I would like to eat so much at once. My favorite, without a doubt, are the birthday cake balls. I don’t see this changing in the future, but I would definitely be open to coming back and trying more… or simply ordering a few dozen of them.

state: I spent countless nights studying and writing assignments here. It’s open 24 hours a day and offers free Wi-Fi, though it can sometimes be slow and difficult to connect to. They also have a great selection of delicious cakes and desserts; I recommend the salty caramel brownies. The coffee here is also of good quality. I haven’t tried the food itself, as I usually prefer cakes more. There’s usually cola available, but most nights, it moves around quite quickly. The place is often full, and it can be hard to find a spot if you’re with a large group, but if there are just a few people, there’s usually something available, either inside or outside one of the many rooms. The decor ensures that there’s always something interesting to see.

state: MACARONS!!! I spent 4 days in Las Vegas and decided to stop here specifically to try these delicious macarons that I’ve always heard about. There’s no secret—macarons are simply divine and irresistible. These were probably the best ones I’ve ever tried. The filling was a bit more creamy, which I loved, as it perfectly contrasted with the crispy and sweet cookies. I spent a little more money and bought two gift boxes: one with mini macarons and another with regular-sized ones. At first, the prices might seem high, but considering the size of the cookies and the quality of the flavor, it’s worth it. In fact, I could only eat most of them when I got home, since I was eating everything else on the Strip haha. To avoid the cookies losing their crunch, I ate my macarons within a few days. However, on the fourth day, I was surprised to find that the cookies were still almost fresh. With experience, I can’t keep macarons edible for more than a day or two (unless they’re eaten immediately!). Next time, I’ll try cupcakes and other options, and hope I don’t stop there with a full stomach. Maybe I’ll come back in a few months?

state: I have been wanting to try this place forever, but I've avoiding it because like ever other local I hate the strip. I was in the Venetian, and accidentally ran into this little gem. I was unprepared, shocked, excited! I knew that I wanted to try the macaroons. At the $3.50 a pop, I could only justify getting one. I settled on my favorite flavor, pistachio, and ordered a chocolate chip cookie as well. The macaroon was overly sweet. To me it tasted like an Andes mint flavored macaroon, so maybe they use mint for color? There was only a subtle hint of pistachio. I was completely disappointed. The macaroons in the freezer section at Walmart are 10 times better. The chocolate chip cookie was okay. The chocolate chips were fantastic, but the cookie was just average. Definitely not something I'd go back for. If you're on the Strip, there are far better options that are more deserving of your money and caloric intake. Skip this one!

state: As soon as you enter, it feels like you’ve traveled back in time and arrived in a luxurious salon. The cakes are beautifully presented, and there’s a wide variety of drinks to choose from. The staff is friendly and moves around carefully behind the counter. Additionally, there’s a parking lot right next to the place—something unusual in Lawrenceville, which is a great advantage! It’s a great place for a quiet conversation on the sofa or in one of the outdoor areas in the garden. The flavors of the cakes are interesting combinations that aren’t usually found in regular bakeries or supermarkets. I gave it one star because, although the cake was delicious, it was a bit heavy. The topping was light and slightly sweet, and the strawberries were fresh. The prices are similar to those of the desserts at Cheesecake Factory. It’s a great place to satisfy your sweet tooth, and you can still feel healthy since the desserts are vegan.

state: At 9:30 p.m., we waited for 20 minutes before being served. We were curious to find out what made these ice creams so special. Don’t plan your order in advance, as they don’t have all the flavors listed on the menu. So, I chose roasted coconut ice cream with marshmallows and Reese’s. It was delicious. The roasted coconut ice cream had a very strong coconut flavor, and I could feel the grated coconut through the ice cream. The atmosphere and the outdoor tables remind me of a college party spot. It’s a simple social environment. Overall, it’s a great place—with one caveat: roasted coconut ice cream wasn’t my first choice, and the place didn’t have all the flavors mentioned on the menu! But it’s a place everyone should visit at least once.

state: Wishing this was a fivestar-er, but man we're bummed. It was hard to find this place at night, no illuminated signage. Once we found it, we were pumped and the girl who welcomed us in was nice. Unfortunately, although we were the only people there... And the only people in the parking lot.. Repeating myself here this joint was not busy, pretty much everything we came for was sold out. The marshmallow you see in every picture on Yelp? Sold Out. What bothers me about that? How do you run out of your signature item, especially when it's (I'm assuming here) not homemade. Go to the grocery store, buy mallows. Problem solved. Same with the red velvet macaroons. I happened to order the last one, leaving my boyfriend to pick from the remaining flavors (Carmel was also sold out). Ice cream flavors were good and the macaroon was tasty, but for $11+ dollars?! No. Especially with the inconvenience of ordering from a limited menu and the atmosphere being kinda meh. Just... No.

state: We closed an evening out with a stop at this open all night bakery. I couldn't believe how many people were waiting in line, but this had to be a good sign, right? The line moved very quickly just as the decisions on what to try had to be made fast. There were 4 of us and together we purchased two vanilla eclairs, two coconut macaroons, chocolate cream puff and raspberry chocolate tart along with fresh brewed coffee. I thought the prices were very reasonable considering the quality. I was told the salted caramel brownies are very popular. The French bohemian decor with mismatched tables, chairs, and odd assortment of pictures on the walls adds to the vibe. Definitely worth stopping in to give yourself a treat.

state: Uncle Bryan came from Los Angeles for the family wedding ceremony. This was a special compliment for Mitchell’s, sent to my nephew Alex… I feel like you’re a little jealous, Alex—which is understandable, considering it’s the best ice cream shop in the world. I’ve been there twice already, and I even have a T-shirt from it. Details: First visit was on July 22nd. I was impressed by the theatrical atmosphere, the abundant light coming from all the windows, the attentive service, the countless forks, and the overall cleanliness inside. It was a bit overwhelming with all the options; I tried Lena’s honey and lavender ice cream—delicious and delicate. Strawberry with pepper? How daring! I chose banana cream ice cream, and I was amazed by the fresh bananas and homemade marshmallow strands. And wait—there’s also homemade cookie base in the ice cream? Yes, there is. This is one of my favorite ice cream spots. Then I was taken upstairs, where I could see the staff working happily in a flawless kitchen through a big window—cutting cookies, brownies. Amazing. I took that sunset photo. We sat at picnic tables and enjoyed those happy summer moments. July 24th. The renowned food critic Xavi attends, and photos of him eating peanut ice cream are sent to me. Trip II: After the wedding, July 25th. Back with the nephews and Topher. As always, pistachio was my favorite ice cream—so I tried roasted pistachio ice cream. Delicious. The nephews are thrilled to get a big portion of ice cream to fill a waffle cone. We observed the work environment. Even with the influence of White Claw, the nephews are still impressed. I mention the slight disappointment that the train isn’t working. But the attendant turns on the switch, and the train starts moving. The nephews deny being reluctant. My only complaint is that the T-shirt isn’t big enough, or maybe I have too many T-shirts from Mitchell’s.

state:
All my favorite places in Los Angeles are finally here in Las Vegas—including the 85°C. It’s just a 25-minute drive from my house; much better than the 4 hours it takes. Cool!! Now, here’s a list of pros and cons to help me and anyone reading this make an informed decision.  

**Pros:**  
1. Of course, all the delicious, soft, and cute desserts. My favorites are brioche, boroh Danish, taro roll bread, Hokkaido cheese cake, and coconut bread. My partner loves all the spicy flavors—jalapeño and cream cheese, hot dog buns, spicy sausage, and ham with cheese.  
2. Due to COVID-19, all desserts come packaged individually. I think this is much easier than the old way. With everything packaged, you don’t have to wait in line for the cashier to pack your desserts one by one, with dirty hands.  
3. I really love their coffee with sea salt foam!! It’s great and gives you a good boost for the day.  

**Cons:**  
1. It’s located in Chinatown. I don’t like Chinatown. People can’t drive there, and Spring Mountain is terrible. It’s in a new, busy shopping center, so good luck finding a parking spot on weekends.  
2. Why is this place so small?! All the other places I’ve visited in Los Angeles were much larger and more spacious. Considering how much they earn, you would think they could afford a bigger space.  
3. Speaking of small spaces, forget about social distance. Customers keep moving around and looking at all the breads, so you’re literally next to someone all the time. And sure, there’s that customer who doesn’t realize how small the space is and takes 19 years to move away.  
4. The line gets very long quickly, and obviously, the careless customer doesn’t know where to go and stands in front of everyone. Why are people so careless?!?! *suspires exasperatedly.* Of course, I’ll go to the hated Chinatown just because of this place. And if you don’t like 85°C, that’s fine. Less people messing up. Thanks, bye!

state: Rewind has a trendy look, but the beauty isn't just skin deep. This is my go to boba place when I'm in Chandler. Layered drinks like the rose milk latte aren't just eye-catching on Instagram-- they're also delicious! I've tried their milk tea and their fruity tea, and they do both well. I would definitely bring anyone here, because they serve things like ice cream and can please people who don't like/aren't willing to try boba. It's also a little cheaper than some other boba places around here. Every time I've been here, the staff have been exceptionally nice. That, coupled with how quickly they make drinks, is what really makes them a five star establishment in my eyes. They also have a good variety of flavors, including non dairy and caffeine free choices, and the ability to customize sugar levels. Someday I'll get ice cream here, but their tea is so good that I haven't been able to not order it!

state: I was very disappointed not having the opportunity to try this place when I visited New York, as it appears in almost all articles that mention things like “25 things you should eat before dying in New York”. So, I was glad to hear that a branch has opened in Las Vegas, a place I visit much more often than in New York. It turns out I wasn’t losing anything. I tried the cereal milk ice cream with cereal pieces, the “crack” cake, the compost cookie, the marshmallow cookie with cornflakes, and the cornflake cookie. The cereal milk ice cream was good; it wasn’t too sweet, and really tasted like milk with soaked cereal. But it’s not something I would want to try again. The “crack” cake – Unfortunately, this cake didn’t live up to its name. It was dry on the outside, soft inside, and extremely sweet. Imagine how a cookie made with butter and too much sugar would taste… Yes. All the cookies were extremely dry and too sweet. Moreover, all these products are very expensive. (The ice cream and “crack” cake cost $6 each, and the cookies cost around $3 each.) In general, the ice cream is worth trying once. It’s not worth buying the cake or cookies.

state: My mother and I walked into sprinkles on a whim while just exploring near our hotel. I sampled the cookie dough ice cream and the captain crunch ice cream. Honestly some of the best ice creams I've ever had . The cookie dough ice cream had big big chunks of cookie dough all throughout the deliciously vanilla flavored ice cream. The captain crunch one tasted just like the cereal and not too sweet with bits of the cereal mixed in. Super smooth and creamy. The waffle cone actually tasted of vanilla and not just processed sugar. My mom got the milk chocolate cupcake . She said she was impressed by how moist it was beautiful texture of the cake and frosting, not too sweet , just the right amount of frosting . She only wishes she got a big "ole" glass of milk with it . And everything wasn't overpriced either ! Next time we are visiting Vegas we will surely be back! Now Candace needs to build a sprinkles in MN !!!

state: This is one of my favorite places to have lunch in the area. They offer a wide variety of options, including soups, salads, and pasta. Their strombolis and pizzas are also excellent. My favorite dishes are basil or artichoke tortellini, or bell pepper Parmesan. The bakery products are great, and it’s hard to choose just one! Special desserts like cheesecakes might be a bit expensive. I’m glad they brought back the donuts, because they’re probably the best donuts I’ve ever eaten. The ice cream is also very good. I love what’s called Donatella – it’s like a version of Ferrero Rocher chocolate, with rice crackers, chocolate, and almonds. Delicious! Presti’s is great for working and observing people. You can get a great coffee and use free Wi-Fi. The only downside is the noise during lunch/dinner. At least you can get a number and be served in order.

state: Whenever I'm in Vegas, I make it a point to have breakfast every day at Bouchon bakery. It's far superior to the Wynn cafe and unsurprisingly, cheaper too! Don't bother with the drip coffee or espresso drinks here; it's like drinking water. I'm also not a fan of their madeleines--they were flavorless and foamy. But everything else I've had? Phenomenal! Try the croissants (especially the STRAWBERRY ones), Parisian macarons (coffee, vanilla, and pistachio are my favs), their muffins, the red velvet cupcake, their focaccia, and the PB&J brioche. The eponymous bouchons are just okay, but are definitely satisfying if all you want is to fulfill a chocolate-y craving.

state: February 24, 2019, Sunday – 21:30, for dessert. 5 adults. Atmosphere: 4 stars. Food: 2 stars. Service: 4 stars. Location: When we entered the Cosmopolitan, we saw ladies with ice cream. They told us we needed to go up to the second floor. Atmosphere: After exiting the elevator, we could see that it’s just a window for buying things. The place isn’t very large. Food and drinks: I ordered the special birthday cake, which means it contains alcohol. I think my expectation of having an adult milk-shake disappeared. But that expectation vanished when I tried to use a wide straw and had difficulty getting any kind of drink. I had to remove the straw several times to eat the birthday cake, as it blocked the straw. Another problem was with vodka; it wasn’t mixed well in the milk-shake. Some portions were good, but the next portion surprised me—it was like high-power fuel. Service: My wife is celiac, and they warned us that the drink we ordered wouldn’t be suitable for celiac people due to the cake. Then I started thinking about what kind of vodka they used. According to the definition, vodka should be made from potatoes and free from gluten, but many distillers use wheat in their vodka. Future: I won’t go back.

state: Today, I decided it was the perfect day to finally visit Sweet Republic. I went with my father and my partner, and the flavor met my expectations. I ordered something simple—the salty, creamy caramel—and paired it with slices of bacon (yes, real bacon slices!). It was delicious, with just the right amount of sweet and salty flavors. The bacon slices weren’t too hard either, both at the beginning and after sitting on top of the ice cream… My partner ordered Toffee Banofi, while my father chose Campfire S’more. Personally, I’m not a big fan of bananas, but my partner loved it, and my father (the biggest ice cream lover in my life) adored it too! I really did… Who wouldn’t get excited after trying homemade malvavisco? Okay, so yes, they prepared the ice cream very quickly (with great effort!). There was plenty of space to sit down, and… we’ll definitely meet up again soon! // Goodbye!//

state: Having been to the original NYC location I knew what to expect when I joined the late night crowd at Milk Bar. I've had the cereal milk soft serve, the pie formerly known as "crack pie", and some of their baked goods. Wanting to try something different, I got a chocolate birthday cake shake, which had pieces of chocolate cake in it and sprinkles. It was actually quite good, probably the best thing that I've tried at Milk Bar. It was rich and thick enough to satisfy a milkshake craving but thin enough to sip easily, sans the cake pieces that got stuck in the straw. When I finished the shake, I wanted more, which is always a good thing. But, after paying $7 for the baby shake, I'm just not sure that I could justify paying more for a larger one.

state: A must-visit when in Charlotte. It's a cute place that is way larger than you would think with quirky eclectic (and a little bit sarcastic) decor that gives the place a cozy feel. It's a little bit on the pricey side in my opinion so be prepared for that however I ordered a meal and 2 desserts: turkey bacon sandwich paired with spinach asparagus leek, a Napoleon and a hazelnut treat. All very good. It was all kind of messy but worth it. My only complaints are dirty tables and the Napoleon which was very good however it didn't cut/break easily and the creme just kinda squished out when pressure applied. I fully intend on returning and trying out more!

state: Visit date: April 11, 2022. After getting a piece of rainbow cake from one of the vending machines throughout the Strip (really, they’re just as common here as Starbucks!), my partner and I decided to buy it directly at Carlo’s Bake Shop, which is located in the Palazzo. It’s possible that we might have to wait for our order, as this place is usually very crowded. However, I don’t like the queue arrangement; it’s difficult to see what you want to order without looking like you’re delaying others. I wish there was a way to see better what’s available before ordering, I think that would improve the flow of people. The staff were friendly, and the cake was amazing; it even stayed fresh for more than a day, since we ate some of it in the hotel room without filling ourselves up too much. Definitely, I would go back and try other products next time we’re here, or just order another piece of this cake.

state: I love this place... it's my hidden gem! I like going here because it's in the cut( not busy) and I like their different flavors and pairings they make. Plus I like the concept of using a fried rice box to put the ice cream in and putting a fortune cookie on top.... PURE GENIUS!!! I like that they ask you if you would like to sample options and the workers are always friendly and kind! Only knock I have which isn't a big one, but still a knock lol is that I usually go late at night(open until 12am) and they either ran out of ice cream options or don't have what I would like! Other than that it's a cool spot to take family, friends, and a date to. I have tried a few different types of their ice creams.. "Reese Puffs".. "Fruity Pebbles".. "Cake Batter"... "Butterfinger".. BOMB.. SUPER BOMB!! So if you have a chance check it out!

state: I was very excited to visit Sinful Sweets, and I even managed to save some calories for several weeks. I had heard about the bacon covered in chocolate, and it seems to be a really creative combination! However, it didn’t meet my expectations. First of all, the bacon wasn’t well-cooked; it was almost raw, and the fat part was still white. Even covered in chocolate, it was awful—I had to spit it out. It was a disappointing day. As for the other desserts, I tried a “turtle” made of pecan nuts and a truffle with chocolate and fruit coating. They were good, but it was hard to appreciate them after the bacon. During my last visit, I chose ice cream, and the carrot cake was really delicious. The service is excellent, very attentive. Maybe I will try them again, after getting over that unpleasant experience with the bacon.

state: Churn offers delicious ice cream flavors, though in a “normal” style. It’s served by two of the most friendly and entertaining ice cream vendors I’ve ever met. In short, two enthusiastic guys greeted my mother and me by saying, “We really enjoy offering samples!” It took me just fourteen seconds to decide that these two were the only people I wanted to interact with every day. So, while I try everything and try not to say the word “love”, the second ice cream vendor tells me that Vietnamese coffee is the perfect choice for mint cookies. To my surprise, I tell him that drinking coffee at this time is dangerous. He says it’s decaffeinated. I make a little animal-like sound. The mint cookies and Vietnamese coffee, perfectly combined in a waffle cone (slightly stale), along with a portion of delicious, unusually light homemade hot chocolate, were really good. However, considering the incredibly pleasant service, the experience goes from “very good” to “incredible”, making Churn one of my favorite places to eat ice cream in Phoenix.

state: Weight watchers beware, this place is simply full of sweets and fattening ice cream sandwiches! You have to admit though that it's a good idea to Treat Yo'self every once in awhile. For those occasions where only delicious desserts will satisfy, I couldn't recommend Ninety's enough! If you're familiar with the boardwalk in the university area then you probably already know where it's at. Park on the side closest to the Light Rail and look for the Chinese restaurant, it's across the walk from there. While there's not much to talk of concerning the decor, it is very clean and there's a bit of seating for people looking to beat the heat. It seems that they're banking on most enjoying their treats on the boardwalk, the rest of the building quickly fills up with excited families and individuals alike wanting a delicious snack. So as far as the treats, what tickles your fancy? They have macaron ice cream sandwiches, ice cream filled doughnuts, ice cream cake pops, all kinds of desserts. You can also get your ice cream in a cup or cone, but why would you? The couple of macaron ice cream sandwiches I've gotten here were outstanding and well thought out. They offer different flavors of macarons paired with specific ice creams and toppings. The team even seems to have a thing for cereals, and incorporates them into a lot of their products! I have to admit, I didn't expect the macarons themselves to be such a high quality product since they're being used in ice cream sandwiches, but I'd say these were excellent macarons. They could even stand on their own with a traditional filling if they chose to do so. Maybe something to consider! I'd love give 'em the perfect score, but last time they were out of a LOT of the specials. They were very accommodating with substitutes, for example they were out of the samoa macaron and just did a regular vanilla on my sandwich. My girlfriend also wanted the coffee ice cream sandwich and they were out of its 'biscotti' macaron so she had to settle for a substitute as well. All in all it they were out of 3 macarons, and 2 ice creams. So I hope that next time I'm able to try some of their named creations as they intended. Still, a very good package either way. Not a gimmick, and still going strong. Way to rock, Ninety's!

state: After hitting Grapes on Shea and Scottsdale for happy hour today- review coming shortly (maybe... hey, I've 12 other reviews that need to be written!), I headed to Sweet Republic for a sweet ending. I'd received a newsletter from SR that there were new flavors in honor of Valentine's Day, and I thought what a great reason to pay SR another visit! Of the two Valentine specials, Raspberry White Chocolate and White Roses, I could only sample the latter, as the former contained an allergen. I'm a sucker for floral-scented food and drink, and this SR delight was a winner! I could definitely taste roses, and the sweet cream wasn't too sweet. Loved it! I also sampled Desert Honey (a tart yogurt sweetened w/ local AZ wild desert honey), Almond Buttercrunch, Salted Butter Caramel, Cheese Course Duo, Espresso, and Mango Lassi. I took a pint of White Roses and Desert Honey ($7.50) and a scoop of Salted Butter Caramel to-go and a scoop of Almond Buttercrunch in a waffle cone (2 scoops $4.25 + $1 for waffle cone) to savor! I couldn't pass up a Chocolate Chip Walnut Oatmeal cookie ($3) as it looked so delicious on its cake display stand- one of the proprietors, Helen, offered to warm it up in the microwave. What a wonderful suggestion! I asked if she could tear off a section and warm it up... The warmed bite I took at the store was amazingly good! (I did notice that the rest of the soft-batch cookie, sampled in the car, was definitely saltier than I'd wish for in a cookie. Why didn't I detect this saltiness in the warmed-up section? Perhaps the sweetness of the almond buttercrunch made my tastebuds more sensitive to salt? Hmm...) I really enjoyed the almond buttercrunch and the cone, so much so that I wished I'd skipped on the salted butter caramel- heresy some fans of this flavor might think, but what can I say? I loved extra textural component, and the buttery toffee-sweet crunch, that the almonds provided. I may be back, maybe as soon as tomorrow!, to re-visit the espresso and the mango lassi (and grab a few more of those chocolate chip walnut cookies!). ;) p.s. Couldn't resist and just had to taste a couple scoopfuls of desert honey and white roses before placing the pint in the freezer... Oh. My. God! Run to SR before Valentine's Day is over and White Roses disappear from the rotation! (Just remember to bring your credit card- a visit could get expensive!)

So, the main drawback is that there aren’t many seats inside, although there are some outside, in the shade. After all, it’s Las Vegas—even in the shade, the temperature is around 34°C! I highly recommend visiting Donut Bar in the center of Las Vegas!

state: I visited 85C Bakery in San Diego in 2017. One of the employees told me that an LV unit was under construction. Two years later, it finally opened! I waited a few days after its opening before visiting, and it was clear that some aspects needed improvement. It was 1 PM, and most of the shelves were empty. They shouted “FRESH BREAD”, but they only produced three different products: BerryTale, Choco Bun, and egg cakes. In the end, I bought some items just because there weren’t many options. The line at the cash register took about 30 minutes. It was Monday, and there were drinks with sea salt in promotion on the app, but when I went to order, the cashier said they didn’t have any promotions, since it was a new store. I came back again, this time at 9 AM. The lines were better, the variety was greater (not just BerryTale boxes), and the “FRESH BREAD” they served was of better quality. In the end, I bought two trays, because I didn’t want to miss out on trying everything. I asked the cashier if they still had any promotions, as I wanted to take advantage of the offer of “buy a $20 gift card and get a free mug”. But last time I visited, they said they didn’t have any. She looked at me confusedly and said they should have informed me about the promotion, and apologized for the incorrect information. In the end, I had dinner at Shanghai Plaza and saw the variety of products. There were still some premium items (I saw someone taking a pink bread, which must be chocolate with strawberries). There was still a line outside, but at least I could see that the shelves were still full of sweets. I have high expectations for 85C, and I think they are still improving their service, as everyone comes to visit and waits in lines. *Tip: there’s a kiosk right in front for ordering drinks and cakes! A girl behind me didn’t get a tray and said she just wanted a drink. One of the women next to her said, “Do you really have to wait in that line for a drink?” I told her about the kiosk, and she went and came back quickly.

state: My favorite ice cream shop of all time. It’s just 5 minutes away by car from my house, and I’ve been going there since I was a child. My family and I go there almost every week. Their ice cream is very creamy, but not too sweet. I usually order the banana flavor—it’s unique. At other times, I try their seasonal flavors; my favorites are the banana with peanut butter (surprise!), the three-fruit flavor, lemon tart, and pumpkin with caramel and ginger cookies in autumn. Also, their orange flower ice cream is perfect for summer—it has a taste similar to a creamsicle, and I’ve never seen it anywhere else. My mother loves the red raspberry sundae. They have branches throughout the Cleveland area, but I grew up going here.

state: The Milk Bar wasn’t as good as I expected. I missed out on knowing where it was located in New York, and I really wanted to try it here in Las Vegas. Not knowing what to order, I decided to try the “Greatest Hits” (19 dollars), which included: a portion of walnut cake, cereal milk ice cream, birthday candies (3 pieces), and a oat cookie. I also bought the cornflake cookie and the chocolate cookie with cornflakes. My least favorite was the cereal milk ice cream with chunks. It really didn’t have much flavor, and it was small in size. The walnut cake was also small. It was a rip-off! The walnut cake was okay, but not impressive. The birthday candies had a strange texture—they seemed too soft, not well-cooked, or made with too much flour. It wasn’t very pleasant. I really wanted to try the birthday cake, but it isn’t sold in portions; it’s only available whole (56 dollars). But I did like the cookies! I might buy them again, but I preferred the cornflake cookies more. A major drawback is that there are no seats or high tables to enjoy the desserts. However, the customer service was excellent. If I’m in the area someday and want to spend money, I might come back for these overpriced treats.

state: Warning: This five-star review is based on extreme nostalgia. When I was young, I insisted that we go here after every zoo visit. Now that I can drive, it surprises me that I don’t go here more often. Honey Hut is the most consistently delicious ice cream in Cleveland. For some, this might seem like a controversial opinion, but I stand by it. I’ve never been here before, and I’ve never been satisfied with the taste, price, or cozy atmosphere of this small shop. This time, I tried the special flavor: banana with chocolate chips. It was quite “banana-like” and had an incredibly fresh taste. My mother chose the classic honey and nuts flavor. In my opinion, this flavor always succeeds. Although it’s very sweet, the nuts balance the taste, allowing you to enjoy it slowly, instead of eating it in two seconds. My sister tried the chocolate and peanut butter ice cream. Even though I’m not a fan of chocolate ice cream, she left with a smile on her face.

During this lockdown, they offer pre-order services that can be completed throughout the week, and picked up on Friday afternoon. It’s exactly what you need for the weekend. Don’t forget to check their Instagram account every week—the availability of products changes weekly. Just go there, call them, and they will deliver to your car without any contact.

The girl behind the counter was very friendly and allowed us to try the flavors we wanted. She was unsure about which flavors I wanted for my ice cream, but she said I could make an ice cream with up to four flavors. She was really excited! state: I had never heard of this place before, but I’ve heard about the exhibition. It’s located inside the Venetian Hotel and Casino, on the second floor. I came here just because my wife insisted. When I saw how long the line was, she had to insist even more, because she couldn’t imagine waiting 45 minutes for a small dessert. While in line, I could hear the women talking and bragging about how much they spent at Carlos’ bakery: 60, 75, 85 dollars! That must be delicious! Some of these women had been here several times. Once you finally get to the front of the line, only a few people are allowed in at a time. BE CAREFUL! Think about what you want, because otherwise, they might leave you waiting or someone behind you might eat you alive. They write down your order, and then you have to wait (another 10 minutes) in one of the 5 seats until they call you to pay. What happened to those bakeries where you just go over, choose what you want, and a Mexican woman puts it in a bag for you? This place forces you to wait while they prepare your desserts in an elegant white box with a ribbon, and they charge a lot of money! “So all the customers’ money goes to the wrapping.” I ordered two small cannoli, one regular and one chocolate. The large cannoli cost $4, while the small ones cost $2.50. They were good, but not exceptional for me. Maybe it’s just the anticipation that didn’t meet my expectations. If the line were shorter and the desserts were a little cheaper, this rating would probably be 4 stars.

Over the past few years, I avoided their original location in Beverly Hills because it didn’t impress me, but I always wanted to try their ice cream. The new location at The Linq on the Las Vegas Strip reminds me a bit of Los Angeles—it has both a cupcake section and an ice cream section. It’s the perfect time to go there in the afternoon (though it’s always hot in Las Vegas, so you can eat ice cream anytime of the day). There are few customers in the cupcake section, and none in the ice cream section. So many flavors—most change daily! So many interesting options; my instinct told me I wanted to try them all. I chose a sample of the only sorbet flavor available—strawberry—and I loved it! It was too good, very refreshing, simply perfect! I came for a red vanilla waffle cone, but I ended up wanting a cupcake sundae instead. I picked a cupcake, it was cut up, and filled with ice cream. I chose the red vanilla one, and I loved it! Very fresh, soft, moist—just what a cupcake should be. The cream cheese frosting had too much sugar; it’s not my favorite, but now I’m convinced it’s not just advertising. Sprinkles makes really good cupcakes, and I’ll definitely try their ice cream again!

state: Sprinkles never disappoints! We saw it from a distance, thanks to its double symbol and “Vegas” style logo. If you travel often, you know what I’m talking about. Anyway, there’s a separate line for cupcakes and ice cream – which was great, because we wanted the ice cream right away, and we got it immediately, while there was a long line for cupcakes on the other side. They also offer regular-sized cupcakes and mini-sundae, which we love! Additionally, the portions are excellent. The service was friendly and quick. The ice cream and mini-cupcakes were great, as always. There are some seats to sit in outside – and if it’s very crowded, there’s a fountain nearby where we can sit too, which we did. I highly recommend it!
